newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.17 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.17 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed in late trading on Friday as traders took advantage of delayed payments to push the IMKB-100 index to a record high close of 97,588.81, up 163.20 or 0.17 percent.
The previous closing record was Thursday's finish of 97,425.62.
The stock market will be closed until January 2. Yesterday's deals will be settled next Thursday and today's next Friday.
In dollar terms, the index stood at 91 cents, unchanged from Thursday, but down from a $1 record on April 8.
The market index surged 143.8 percent from last year's close of 40,024.57. In dollar terms, the rise was 35.8 percent from the end-1995 close of $0.67.
Brokers said trade was quiet due to weak volume which dived to 11.40 trillion lira from Thurday's 14.85 trillion.
"Trade was unexpectedly dull for the year's last session, but some buying emerged towards the close to push the index above the 97,000 level," said Erol Guney from Yurtbank.

The government on Thursday extended the holiday to five days to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday in the public sector. The Exchange afterwards said the market would be closed on Monday and Tuesday and settlements would be delayed to after the holiday.
The index had leapt 2.84 percent on Thursday on buying fuelled by the delay in payments. Most investors place their funds in repo deals on the bond market over the holiday.
The market index rose 3.32 percent this week after a 6.2 percent surge last week.

Of the 231 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 105 to 69 and 57 were stable. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.33 percent to 104,590.86 while the 15-share financial index eased 0.21 percent to 91,446.89.

Actives were led by utility Aktas Elektrik, down 1,000 lira at 95,000 and largely state owned firms -- petroleum refiner Tupras, down 500 lira at 27,000 and flat steel producer Eregli, steady at 13,000 lira. Together, they made up 25.4 percent of the total turnover.
